note: Official-behaviour claims (ids <area>-O<n>), community claims (<area>-C<n>), action requirements (github-actions-A<n>) and inline verifications (<area>-I<n>). Each locator is re-checkable: a repository file at a full commit SHA with lines, a CHANGELOG line at the v2.1.295 tag, a documentation URL with its fetch time and the sha256 of the bytes read, or a read-only installed-client command.

claims.claim: Use an Agent call for one delegated task, a skill for reusable judgment, and a native dynamic workflow when required ordering and structured handoffs need orchestration.
claims.note: One authored routing guide; native background-workflows-O5/O6/O7 already supplies the orchestration runtime and result retention; its zero-orchestrator-token assertion is limited to script execution and does not mean model-backed agent calls are free.

claims.claim: Keep one primary completion-loop authority and use artifact-only checkpoints when a second loop would conflict with the active runtime.
claims.note: OMC explicitly chooses among native /goal and package loops, while CE bounds one mutated target and one watcher; this is two independently authored coordination policies, not evidence to replace native scheduling-O11 with a whole framework.

claims.claim: The installed --bg or --background flag returns a background-session ID immediately and combines with --resume to continue the same session unless an already running session requires an announced copy.

Background sessions waiting on a scheduled wakeup stay running through updates and low memory, while on macOS or Linux without an installed background service stopping claude agents together with its service stops running sessions in about a minute unless agent view is reopened.
The installed claude agents --json command prints active interactive and background sessions without a TTY, and --all adds completed background sessions.

A supervisor hosts full background conversations after the terminal closes, keeps active or permission-waiting sessions running, and may stop an unattached idle process after about an hour while preserving its conversation.

On background-session process exit or restart, background shell commands, workflows, and subagents carry over while monitors and subagent-started shell commands stop, and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BG_EXIT_HANDOFF=1 makes all of that work stop with the process.

A dynamic workflow executes a JavaScript orchestration script in a separate background runtime whose intermediate results stay in variables and whose filesystem and shell operations are delegated to agents.
Workflow concurrency defaults to at most 16 agents subject to available CPUs, can be set from 1 to 256, and each run permits at most 4096 items per parallel or pipeline call and 1000 total agents.
The workflow runtime retains completed agent results so an interrupted run can resume within the same session.
A forked skill invoked by a Workflow subagent delivers its result to that invoking agent rather than the main conversation.
When Workflow scriptPath is refused because the session lacks a Read tool, the refusal identifies inline script as the usable route.
Use rewind to restore or summarize the appropriate conversation and tracked file changes, and use Git checkpoints for broader risky edits.
claims.note: Both advice streams reuse native checkpoint guidance and count once; checkpoints-rewind-O1/O2/O3 limits restoration to tracked file-tool edits, excluding Bash and most subagent edits; a Git commit does not become a native rewind checkpoint.

claims.claim: Claude Code checkpoints file-tool edits before each prompt that starts a turn, retains snapshots for the 100 most recent checkpoints and saves them with the session, with the default cleanup sweep deleting snapshots about 30 days after the last saved one.
claims.note: A queued message that joins an existing turn does not create its own checkpoint; see lines 93-97.

claims.claim: The /rewind or empty-input Esc Esc menu can restore code, conversation or both and summarize before or after a chosen prompt, with code restore offered only where tracked changes exist.
claims.note: The summarize choices alter context rather than reverting files.

claims.claim: Checkpointing excludes Bash-driven and external edits and most subagent edits, while foreground forked skills running during the parent turn are the documented subagent restoration exception.
claims.note: Session checkpoints support recovery alongside version control; they do not replace Git history.

claims.claim: Rewind skips tracked symlinked or hard-linked paths, and debug logging identifies the paths and reasons skipped.
When /compact, /clear or /rewind is entered while viewing a background agent or teammate transcript, a dialog names the target conversation and asks before changing it.
The rewind menu lists prompts submitted while Claude was still working.
claims.note: Listing a queued prompt does not imply that a mid-turn message has its own file checkpoint; current docs distinguish turn-start checkpoints.

claims.claim: A prompt sent after /rewind is preserved and removed turns remain removed when the session moves to the background or resumes after being killed.
Stopped scheduled tasks remain stopped after rewind and resume, while active tasks are no longer lost when resuming after Esc or rewind following compaction.
claims.note: Scheduling state correctness is part of the documented rewind/resume fix; no scheduled task was run.

claims.claim: Shan's quick tips propose universal context-quality boundaries near 300–400K tokens or 40% utilization, and the guide separately proposes manual compaction at 70%.
claims.note: These are attributed heuristics, not current client thresholds or source-published per-task quality studies; native context-token-O1/O8 gives model-specific compaction and natural task-break guidance, while the guide itself says percentage is not a validated reasoning-quality threshold at line 841.

claims.claim: Cache-aware guidance preserves stable prompt prefixes and keeps variable context in appended or live-zone content.
claims.note: Independent sources agree on prefix preservation as architecture, not on a universal savings number; context-token-O9/O10/O13 is the native source of truth for prefix matching, effort changes and deferred MCP tools.

claims.claim: Context Mode executes analysis outside the conversation and retrieves selected indexed sections rather than returning the raw payload to the model.
claims.note: The published 21-scenario 376KB-to-16.5KB report gives 96% context reduction and 100% code-example preservation, but no paired model task-quality outcome; the numeric saving is quality-unmeasured.

claims.claim: RTK compresses shell output while describing its token counts as bytes divided by four and its output reductions as distinct from billing reductions.
claims.note: The up-to-90% number is shell-output reduction, not provider-token or invoice savings, and the cited source reports no paired task-quality outcome; quality-unmeasured. The guide declares its author is an RTK core contributor, so that guide is not an independent RTK effectiveness vote.

claims.claim: Caveman's published wrap benchmark reports lower provider input at held exact-answer quality across deterministic tool-output fixtures.
claims.note: The report gives 33.2% lower input, 18/18 direct and Caveman exact checks, 18 matched pairs/54 total runs, six fixtures and a 14.6–48.5% case-bootstrap interval on Claude Code 2.1.223/Sonnet 5; its raw harness/run artifacts are absent, so it is a source-reviewed measured report and cannot be independently reproduced from this checkout.

claims.claim: Headroom retains recoverable originals and reports tokenizer-based compression and task accuracy with explicit workload-dependent limits.
claims.note: The four MCP-payload reduction scenarios (21–57%) and four N=100 accuracy tasks are separate tables and are not a matched end-to-end cost/quality result; they cannot establish one held-quality saving. The source says the +0.03 TruthfulQA delta is inside its confidence interval, not a detectable improvement.

claims.claim: Claude-Mem uses search for compact IDs, timeline for context and get_observations only for filtered results.
claims.note: The ~10x token-saving assertion has no task sample, actual provider counters, comparison protocol or quality result in the cited passage, so it is quality-unmeasured.

claims.claim: Compound Engineering loads skill details by phase and reports reduced always-loaded skill bytes alongside bounded fresh-host behavior checks.
claims.note: The source reports ce-plan 31,069→6,899 bytes, ce-work 27,859→7,029 bytes and 27/27 narrow catalog behavior grades across Claude/Codex/Grok; these are source-reported contract/required-read checks, not task-completion quality or a provider-token cost experiment.

claims.claim: Native one-million-token models normally compact at about 967K tokens, and the official model-specific thresholds do not establish a universal 300–400K quality boundary.
claims.note: The quality-boundary assertion was not found in the cited model threshold section; no model-quality experiment was run.

claims.claim: Effort changes preserve cache on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5.1 with API-key or subscription authentication, with documented exceptions for Bedrock, Agent Platform, the Claude apps gateway, disabled experimental betas and HIPAA configurations.
claims.note: The platform distinction is top-level effort versus supported per-message effort; cache-preserving client behavior must not be generalized to arbitrary API requests or gateways.

claims.claim: The default main-conversation cache TTL is one hour for included Claude subscription usage and five minutes for API-key, cloud-provider or usage-credit billing, while most outside-conversation requests default to five minutes.

TTL precedence is forced five-minute caching, bucket environment variable, bucket setting, subagent experimental.cacheTtl, global one-hour enablement, then the billing-dependent default, and a subagent frontmatter hour is ignored while subscription usage credits pay for it.

With tool search deferral active an MCP server change can preserve the cached prefix, while upfront tool definitions behind custom gateways can invalidate it, and toggling the advisor preserves the prefix because its definition follows the cache breakpoint.

Since 2.1.288 the first request after fresh startup or a model switch uses server-reported output and auto-compact limits rather than built-in defaults, with up to a 1.5-second wait, and 2.1.285 corrected SDK setModel limit refresh.
In 2.1.288 zero reported token usage no longer prevents automatic compaction, and 2.1.284 adds another smaller compaction when the first compacted request remains too long.
In 2.1.293 the compaction summary no longer makes Claude misread its own immediately preceding actions as completed after compaction and retract or repeat finished work.
In 2.1.295 a one-million-token request rejected by a gateway or cloud provider for its context-1m beta is retried without that beta.
In 2.1.290 resumed subagents and teammates keep their previous thinking and prompt cache after receiving a message mid-run.
Increasing CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS reduces the effective input context available before auto-compaction, and values above a model's output cap are lowered to that cap.

Since 2.1.285 a custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL uses the native one-million-token context of recognized capable models, and since 2.1.287 Opus 4.7+ and Fable also default to that window on Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry and the Claude apps gateway.
Since 2.1.288 /autocompact saves the auto-compact window separately for each model, with the current model's saved value taking precedence over a same-file global window.

CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE can lower the early-compaction trigger for main conversations and subagents but cannot raise the default threshold and applies only to sessions that compact before the model limit.
DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT disables automatic compaction while preserving manual /compact, whereas DISABLE_COMPACT disables both automatic and manual compaction.

Compaction re-injects project-root CLAUDE.md, unscoped rules and auto memory from disk, reloads nested and path-scoped instructions on demand, and summarizes earlier hook context unless a compact SessionStart hook adds it again.
Compaction re-injects invoked skill bodies subject to a 5,000-token per-skill and 25,000-token total cap, dropping oldest skills first, and re-reads up to five recently modified session files.
The official guidance is to compact with a stated focus at natural task breaks, while /rewind can retain an already cached prefix instead of rebuilding the conversation layer through compaction.
Prompt caching matches an exact request prefix, so a system-prompt change invalidates later layers while appended plan or skill instructions preserve the earlier prefix.
Session-metrics distinguishes token buckets and cache TTLs while labeling per-turn dollar values as estimates.
claims.note: Native cost-usage-O1 makes Claude Console authoritative for API billing; this source's raw JSONL metrics add reporting views without converting estimated costs into invoices.

claims.claim: A compression decision should keep output-byte reduction, provider input including cache buckets and priced cost as separate reported metrics.
claims.note: Independent primary sources distinguish these quantities: RTK uses bytes/4 and Caveman sums input/cache-read/cache-creation counters without price weighting. Their metrics cannot be combined into one cost-saving percentage.

claims.claim: Compound Engineering's review-spine evaluation tracks ordered behavior gates, orchestration turns and exposed cache usage in four source-reported live host runs.
claims.note: Two runs per Claude/Codex host cover focused/full paths; full Claude cache-write changes 942k→739k and cache-read12.5M→6.49M compare with a historical baseline. Codex per-turn usage is unavailable, and live peer failure/lite gates were not exercised, so this is narrow behavior-plus-cache evidence rather than a general per-task saving.

claims.claim: Model and prompt-steering comparisons should read compliance changes together with cost changes while preserving the limits of the quality proxy.
claims.note: The source documents a fixed ten-prompt IFEval-style method and warns that steering changes strict format pass rates; no current route, model winner or general coding quality gain is established.

claims.claim: The /usage session dollar total is a locally computed token-price estimate, optionally using managed modelPricing, and authoritative API billing remains in the Claude Console.

In 2.1.288 blocked-on-user telemetry reports correct source and decision for print/SDK sessions and PreToolUse approvals, and 2.1.293 caps each prompt's agent and MCP-resource at-mention events at 100 apiece.
In 2.1.286 /usage attributes an MCP tool result even when its server is still connecting or has only just connected.
The /insights command analyzes recent local sessions through the same provider and account, writes an HTML workflow report, and charges its analysis tokens to that plan or API usage.
The Prompt cache (main) /usage line and matching status-line prompt_cache object report main-conversation API cache fields, exclude subagents, and reset with /clear.

OpenTelemetry cost and token counters increment after each API request and expose model, effort, speed and query_source attribution, with token input excluding separately counted cacheRead and cacheCreation tokens.

Advisor calls consume additional tokens at the advisor model's rates and count toward /usage session totals, with subscription limits or usage-credit billing depending on the account and selected advisor.
In 2.1.285 /cost and SDK modelUsage attribute refusal-fallback turns to the model that actually served them rather than the client's predicted fallback model.

Since 2.1.284 gateway spend limits in /usage and the status line include dollar amounts and used_usd, limit_usd and period fields when the gateway server also runs 2.1.284 or later, and 2.1.295 keeps those limits visible with nonessential traffic disabled.
In 2.1.286 the Claude apps gateway spend meter prices hour-long cache writes correctly and counts input across streamed server-tool calls rather than only the first model call.
Since 2.1.287 OpenTelemetry user_prompt includes prompt_text as an alias of prompt under the same redaction gate, so collectors that drop or mask prompt must treat both attributes.
OpenTelemetry prompt text, tool arguments and tool content are redacted by default, with separate OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS, OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS and OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT opt-ins.
GitHub recommends full-length commit SHA references as immutable action versions, and the pinned Claude action also uses full SHAs for its Bun and Node setup actions.
claims.note: Pinned action dependencies are source pins; the native Claude installer fetched at runtime remains a separate boundary.

claims.claim: GitHub rulesets can require status checks from a selected integration, resolved conversations, linear history and code-scanning results, and can specify bypass actors independently for each ruleset.
claims.note: The number of reviews and checks, strict up-to-date behavior and bypass choice are repository policy choices rather than a universal GitHub default.

claims.claim: Claude Code Action v1.0.247 supports direct Anthropic API workload identity federation using a federation rule and organization, with optional service-account and workspace selectors, and needs id-token: write for that exchange.
claims.note: Legacy API-key and subscription OAuth inputs also exist upstream; these reviewed workflows select federation only.

claims.claim: At v1.0.247, direct Anthropic API workload identity federation supports authentication without a static API key when anthropic_federation_rule_id, anthropic_organization_id and job id-token: write permission are configured.
Omit anthropic_api_key and claude_code_oauth_token when using workload identity federation because either static credential takes precedence and disables the federation setup.
Use the Anthropic audience https://api.anthropic.com by default, with optional service account, workspace and custom audience inputs as appropriate for the federation rule.

For cloud providers, use the documented OIDC paths for AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI or Microsoft Foundry and configure the respective cloud login before selecting use_bedrock, use_vertex or use_foundry.
claims.note: The examples use mutable action tags; they establish provider wiring, not compliance with full-SHA pinning.

claims.claim: Distinguish Claude API federation from the action's separate GitHub App token exchange, which requests the claude-code-github-action audience when no explicit github_token is supplied.

GitHub withholds repository secrets and limits GITHUB_TOKEN on fork pull_request runs, while pull_request_target and workflow_run use the base repository context, so untrusted heads must remain data and actor exceptions must be narrowly scoped.
claims.note: Allowed bots bypass the repository write gate after the actor-type check; allowed_non_write_users requires an explicit workflow token and introduces documented risk.

claims.claim: Retain the default write-permission gate for issue, pull-request, comment and review contexts and workflow_run contexts, accepting human actors only when the collaborator API reports admin or write.

Keep allowed_bots empty unless a specific trusted App is needed, because bot matching bypasses repository write-permission checks and an allowed external App can trigger public-repository events without installation or write access.
claims.note: Both tag and agent modes call checkHumanActor; the separate write gate accepts [bot] actors, while non-suffix non-user actors are matched by allowed_bots in the API error path.

claims.claim: Do not use allowed_non_write_users for these trusted review flows because it bypasses the human write gate only when an explicit github_token is supplied and can admit all actors with the wildcard value.
If a deliberately limited non-write-user workflow is adopted, supply the ephemeral job GITHUB_TOKEN rather than a personal access token and minimize its permissions and allowed tools.
claims.note: The documented subprocess secret scrub is best effort, may be opted out, and does not prove that prompt injection cannot reach credentials.

claims.claim: Check both the workflow actor and the actor that started an upstream workflow_run when they differ, so a maintainer downstream actor alone does not authorize a non-write upstream contributor.

Keep an untrusted PR head out of the workspace root for pull_request_target or workflow_run jobs that expose base-repository secrets, using the trusted base checkout and the documented separate PR directory pattern instead.
claims.note: Actor authorization and default bot controls do not constitute an unconditional fork exclusion.

claims.claim: Treat the remaining PR working-tree files as untrusted even after the action restores its fixed base-branch Claude configuration paths, and keep trusted hooks and helpers independent of PR-controlled scripts and executable project configuration.
claims.note: The fixed restore set is .claude/, .mcp.json, .claude.json, .gitmodules, .ripgreprc, CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md and .husky/.

claims.claim: The action defaults show_full_output and display_report to false, but ACTIONS_STEP_DEBUG=true forces full SDK output and the retained execution_file contains complete unredacted messages.
claims.note: Public-log hardening must prevent debug activation and avoid printing or uploading the execution file; an intentional final review in a job summary is distinct from a transcript.

claims.claim: Keep show_full_output false because full output serializes all SDK messages, including assistant content and tool execution results, into publicly visible Actions logs.
Reject effective ACTIONS_STEP_DEBUG=true before action execution because parseSdkOptions automatically enables full output even when show_full_output is false.
Keep display_report false because enabling it writes Claude-authored assistant and tool content to GitHub Step Summary and can fall back to a redacted raw execution JSON report.
claims.note: Default at v1.0.247 is false; no default-true claim is made.

claims.claim: Do not publish the execution_file through log printing or public artifacts because the action saves the full unsanitized SDK messages to claude-execution-output.json irrespective of console full-output settings.
Keep workflow prompts and SDK option values suitable for public logs because the action logs its context prompt and SDK options without env or extraArgs even when full SDK message output is hidden.
claims.note: The action's own fixed progress and context logs cannot be removed by show_full_output:false; avoid placing sensitive material in those values.

claims.claim: Treat runner.debug and RUNNER_DEBUG as step-debug indicators rather than proof that runner diagnostic logging is disabled, because the runner derives that context from Step_Debug and independently enables diagnostic log upload from RunnerDebug.
claims.note: Verified at current actions/runner HEAD 67f01c276e0a91d967ba499ce4cdc9a95efa0262, not a recorded live GitHub-hosted runner execution.

claims.claim: The GitHub runner sets runner.debug from its step-debug flag, so that context alone does not prove runner diagnostic logging is disabled.

Supply an explicitly permission-scoped job github_token when the workflow must rely on job permissions for GitHub access, because the default action path independently exchanges an OIDC token for a GitHub App token.
claims.note: Job permissions scope the job GITHUB_TOKEN; the independent App exchange's actual server-granted scopes were not queried.

claims.claim: Account for the App token client's contents, pull_requests and issues write defaults when using additional_permissions, since the parser merges additional entries over those defaults and sends the result to the exchange service.
claims.note: When additional_permissions is absent, the client omits the permissions body rather than sending DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS; service default scope is not proved by this source alone.

claims.claim: Grant only the GitHub API operations the chosen flow actually needs, considering the official App's content, pull-request and issue read/write capabilities.
claims.note: The parent's requirement R5 should cross-check live PR job permissions and whether a provided GITHUB_TOKEN or independently minted App token is used.

claims.claim: GitHub recommends granting GITHUB_TOKEN only necessary job permissions; passing it explicitly to this action skips the independently minted GitHub App token, and checkout offers persist-credentials:false to opt out of stored git authentication.
claims.note: id-token:write issues an OIDC identity token; it does not grant repository write access. App-token scopes are separate from workflow GITHUB_TOKEN scopes.

claims.claim: The action ships PR review, security-focused review, manual analysis and issue-triage examples; model and effort are supported CLI arguments, and native Claude prompt caching is enabled unless disabled by its documented environment controls.
claims.note: Examples are capability demonstrations, not a mandate to copy broad token scopes, static keys or tag refs. Explicit model/effort is the review configuration criterion.

claims.claim: Prompt-cache hits require identical eligible prompt prefixes and model-specific minimum lengths; the API can validly return zero cache-read tokens, so usage counters establish observed reuse rather than a universal success invariant.
claims.note: These PRs deliberately enforce a positive cache read as a local acceptance bound. This is stricter than upstream; no new cache mechanism is needed for native Claude.

claims.claim: GitHub scheduled workflows run from the default branch and may be delayed or disabled after 60 days of inactivity on public repositories, while Dependabot GitHub Actions updates target declared action dependencies.
claims.note: A configured source-HEAD watch, release query and a successful scheduled execution are different kinds of evidence.

claims.claim: Separate on-demand PR review and issue-label triage, then bind review conclusions to the reviewed revision and the repository's required checks.
claims.note: Guide triggers and permissions are examples, not current action-runtime acceptance; CE independently requires live PR snapshots and bounded actions; source examples use mutable @v1, so immutable action pins must be qualified by the action lane rather than inferred from community prevalence.

claims.claim: Default a code-review procedure to findings only and make local application, posting, pushing and merging separate authorized effects.
claims.note: CE, Loop and the guide support bounded review but davila7's selected PR command explicitly posts and immediately applies all recommendations; this is real source dissent, not universal advisory behavior or a requirement for a second human before every merge; native slash-commands-O10/O12 covers native review controls.

claims.claim: Main's required status checks are seven (validate, token-report, secret-scan, dependency-review, osv-scanner, verdict-review-gate, sota-sources); validate-macos left the list on 2026-10-05.
Use print mode with an explicit structured-output contract for scripted analysis and qualify the actual flags at the installed client version.
claims.note: Native headless-sdk-O1 supplies text/json/stream-json; piped input examples are workflow recipes rather than live executions; the generic timeout example is corrected in headless-sdk-C2.

claims.claim: A print-mode build can be time-bounded with the generic claude -p --timeout 300 example.
claims.note: Native headless-sdk-O16 records scoped negative evidence at 2.1.295; this does not mean the separate ultrareview --timeout is absent, and no model-backed command was run.

claims.claim: Use bare mode only after qualifying its explicit API-key or helper authentication route and its omitted hooks, memory and auto-discovered configuration.
claims.note: Native headless-sdk-O2/O3 covers the current behavior; bare mode omits multiple runtime components rather than proving model output deterministic; the source recipe requires an API key, and no credential was read or bare call made.

claims.claim: Print mode skips the workspace trust dialog and silently ignores settings files that fail validation, and its output formats are text, one JSON result, or stream-json events.
The TypeScript SDK defaults to a minimal system prompt unless systemPrompt explicitly requests the claude_code preset or supplies a custom prompt.

A print run normally caps continuous idle background waiting at ten minutes, configurable with CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS, but a main-started running background command and a text-prompt self-paced loop can keep it open past that cap.

Since 2.1.285 print and Python Agent SDK sessions on third-party providers or with telemetry disabled start in auto mode if no permission mode is configured, while an explicit --permission-mode overrides that default.
In 2.1.295 a print run writes a terminal stderr notice explaining what it is waiting for when it remains open after its last turn.

The --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections flag moves per-user dynamic context to the first user message to improve cross-user cache reuse and is ignored with a custom system prompt or system-prompt file.
The --session-id flag requires a valid UUID, while print-mode --max-turns defaults to unlimited and errors at an explicit cap, with queued stream-json messages starting a new turn with a fresh limit.
A general --timeout flag was not found in the installed 2.1.295 top-level help or the official CLI flag table, although the documented ultrareview subcommand has its own --timeout option.
claims.note: This scoped negative describes the sources read, not an exhaustive search of hidden client switches or SDK runtime controls.

claims.claim: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB strips recognized credentials from child Bash, hook and stdio-MCP environments while preserving GitHub tokens and proxy settings, and the parent keeps its API credentials.
A mandated commit-message format was not found in the installed 2.1.295 CLI help or the official CLI-reference command and flag tables read for this inventory.
claims.note: This does not search every native plugin or claim that Claude Code cannot follow a repository's existing commit convention; it leaves the baseline's efficacy/rejection disposition outside this documentary review.

claims.claim: Bare mode skips configured hooks, plugin synchronization, attribution, auto-memory, background prefetches, keychain reads and CLAUDE.md discovery, and Anthropic authentication uses an API key or explicitly supplied apiKeyHelper rather than OAuth.
Since 2.1.286 bare sessions connect only command-line MCP servers, omit system reminders, start no background tasks, and stop a timed-out shell command instead of backgrounding it.

Restricted mode removes command and code execution tools and WebFetch unless explicitly named, skips user/project/local settings, confines file tools to working directories, and refuses bypassPermissions while retaining managed and explicit settings.
In 2.1.295 the --tools and --restricted limits also apply to built-in tools registered after launch, and deprecated names cannot reach tools outside the caller's tool set.
The pinned Python Agent SDK bundles Claude Code by default and accepts cli_path to select a separately installed client.
Python query returns an asynchronous iterator of response messages, while ClaudeSDKClient provides bidirectional interactive conversations.

The SDK allowed_tools/allowedTools options auto-approve named tools without restricting the available toolset, whereas disallowed tools block matching operations and bare tool names remove tool definitions.

Omitted SDK setting_sources/settingSources normally uses all CLI filesystem sources, except Python loads only user and project sources when skills is set and setting_sources is omitted, while an explicit empty source list skips user/project/local settings without disabling endpoint-managed policy.
Put narrow deterministic preconditions in hooks, parse event JSON explicitly, and test pass, deny and malformed fixtures.
claims.note: Guide hook mechanics match native hooks-O3/O4/O9; the harness supplies independently authored runtime-rule layers but does not prove every host intercepts every effect; two policy implementations agree on external gates, with runtime efficacy not measured here.

claims.claim: Use PostToolUse formatting hooks for repeatable formatting while checking each template against the current event payload.
claims.note: One vendor-derived recommendation plus an authored template; the template depends on CLAUDE_TOOL_FILE_PATH and suppresses command errors, whereas hooks-O3 documents JSON stdin, so source presence is not an executed integration check and no working-formatter claim is made.

claims.claim: Choose notification events according to whether the signal means a completed response or a waiting permission prompt.
claims.note: The template uses Stop for completion and is not evidence of permission-prompt coverage; native hooks-O14 defines the separate waiting Notification behavior; one implementation, no success-rate or latency measurement.

claims.claim: Bind completion to concrete checks and stop or escalate bounded retry loops when checks remain failing or unknown.
claims.note: Three independently authored packages agree on evidence and bounded completion, although their exact loop authorities differ; native scheduling-O11 and hooks-O3 cover goal/Stop primitives, while packages add ledgers or PR-state policies; no claim of a universal benefit from standing verifier prose is inferred.

claims.claim: Hooks can be configured in user, project, local and managed settings or plugins and skill/agent frontmatter, and handlers support command, HTTP, MCP tool, prompt and experimental agent types.
InstructionsLoaded reports agent_id and agent_type when subagent file access loads rules or nested CLAUDE.md, and file-access instruction loads also report effort.
Sandboxed Bash commands on Linux no longer trigger ConfigChange hooks or reload settings mid-command solely because .claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.local.json is absent.
claims.note: The documented correction concerns nonexistent settings files, not a prohibition on real configuration-change events.

claims.claim: A PreCompact hook can block compaction with exit code 2 or decision:block, causing proactive automatic compaction to be skipped but context-limit recovery compaction to surface the API error and fail the current request.
claims.note: For manual /compact the blocking stderr message is displayed; the hook's systemMessage and continue fields are discarded.

claims.claim: Exit-0 PreCompact stdout being appended as compaction instructions was not found in the retained hooks.md PreCompact/output sections or hooks-guide.md compaction guidance.
claims.note: The retained tagged CHANGELOG's PreCompact entries at lines 5736 and 8311 describe blocking support and the event's addition, not this stdout instruction behaviour; this bounded absence does not prove the client lacks it.

claims.claim: Notification hooks receive permission_prompt after a prompt has waited about six seconds and still fire when preferredNotifChannel disables local alerts, whose default is auto with configurable bell or terminal-specific desktop notification channels.
claims.note: PermissionRequest supplies the immediate tool-permission signal; Notification permission_prompt also covers a sandbox network approval prompt, for which PermissionRequest does not run; preferredNotifChannel controls alert delivery rather than the hook event, and its documented values are auto, terminal_bell, iterm2, iterm2_with_bell, kitty, ghostty and notifications_disabled.

claims.claim: Hook matchers use exact names or name lists for simple patterns and unanchored JavaScript regular expressions for other patterns, while all matching handlers run in parallel and duplicate settings-file handlers run once.
claims.note: Plugin and skill copies are kept separate; parallel hooks that rewrite the same input can finish in nondeterministic order.

claims.claim: Command hooks receive event JSON on stdin and communicate through JSON stdout, stderr and exit codes, with exit 2 blocking on blocking-capable events and PostToolUse unable to undo an action already performed.
claims.note: A parsed blocking JSON decision can be honored independently of exit status under the event's documented decision model.

claims.claim: PreToolUse hooks run before permission-mode checks even in dontAsk or bypassPermissions, but an allow decision cannot override deny or ask rules or required interactive MCP approvals.
PermissionRequest hooks run when a call is about to prompt and also in sessions unable to show a prompt, where absence of a hook decision leaves the call denied.

Only command hooks support async:true, which continues the session without waiting, cannot block or steer the already-running action, and delivers output on a later turn while the session remains alive.
claims.note: Ordinary async output waits for the next interaction when idle; asyncRewake exit 2 is the documented wakeup exception.

claims.claim: Edits to hook settings are normally picked up by the file watcher automatically, with restarting the session documented as recovery if a change is missed.
claims.note: The source does not require restarting after every edit.

claims.claim: SessionStart, Setup, CwdChanged and FileChanged hooks can append exports to CLAUDE_ENV_FILE to persist variables for subsequent Bash commands.
claims.note: This describes the documented persistence mechanism; no hook or shell environment was changed.

claims.claim: Command and HTTP hooks can set onFailure:"block" so failure to start, timeout or an unexpected exit code blocks the action instead of allowing it through.
claims.note: The field was not found in the retained hooks.md or hooks-guide.md pages; the exact 2.1.295 CHANGELOG line is the source.

claims.claim: The guide recommends selective MCP use and the native ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH threshold instead of assuming every connected server's full schema loads eagerly.
claims.note: Native mcp-O2 confirms the default 10% auto threshold, with proxy/model fallback boundaries; the source's 85% historical schema reduction is not a paired task-quality measurement.

claims.claim: Agent definitions can restrict tools to the role's needs, as the VoltAgent context manager omits Bash while template context management uses an explicit smaller tool list.
claims.note: Native subagents-teams-O1 already implements tools/disallowedTools; these definitions demonstrate allowlists, not measured token or quality benefits. Templates' agent catalogue credits wshobson/agents at README.md:144-168, so copied catalogue material is not counted as another independent origin.

claims.claim: The templates repository offers an enabledMcpjsonServers preset that enables only named project servers.
claims.note: The two sources agree on selective configuration; neither supplies a matched role-specific tool-set experiment or task-quality metric. Project selection still uses native MCP configuration.

claims.claim: The scoped source sample documents remote HTTP MCP endpoints and a local HTTP memory worker but does not establish one shared HTTP MCP process across sessions as a quality-measured community default.
claims.note: HTTP transport support and an HTTP worker API are separate from evidence of cross-session MCP pooling; no independent measured adoption was verified in this bounded review.

claims.claim: Local and user MCP scopes live in ~/.claude.json and project scope in .mcp.json, with duplicate server entries resolved as whole entries in local, project then user precedence.
claims.note: Fields from duplicate entries are not merged.

claims.claim: A non-interactive first turn still waits up to two seconds for connecting MCP servers named by --allowedTools or an mcp_tool hook even when CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_STARTUP_WAIT_MS=0.
MCP resources are attached through @server:protocol://resource/path references and server prompts appear as slash commands such as /mcp__github__pr_review.
claims.note: Prompts from the reserved anthropic-skills server name are not listed, although its tools remain available.

claims.claim: MCP tool search normally defers schemas until needed, ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=auto uses a 10% context threshold and auto:N a custom threshold, and documented unsupported model or proxy configurations fall back to loading upfront.
claims.note: The default unset value is documented as all tools deferred, not threshold mode; ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false loads upfront.

claims.claim: MCP results warn above 10,000 tokens and default to a 25,000-token limit controlled by MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS, with oversized successful text-only results saved to session tool-results files.
claims.note: A tool's anthropic/maxResultSizeChars text limit supersedes the environment limit for its text; image content remains subject to the token cap.

claims.claim: An MCP server's alwaysLoad:true loads tools upfront and waits up to the standard five-second connection timeout, while per-tool upfront metadata alone does not make startup wait.
claims.note: A valid remote cached entry supplies tools without delaying startup.

claims.claim: A tool's _meta['anthropic/alwaysLoad']=false stays deferred under an alwaysLoad server supplied through --mcp-config, the Agent SDK or a plugin, and server alwaysLoad:false defers every tool including author-marked upfront tools.
claims.note: The per-tool opt-out correction landed in 2.1.285 at line 913; whole-server forced deferral landed in 2.1.287 at line 712.

claims.claim: Descriptions of tools loaded through MCP tool search are clipped at 16,384 characters rather than 2,048.

Local stdio MCP connections negotiate protocol 2026-07-28 by default on all installs, and claude.ai connectors use that default when installs fetch no flags, with MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION=legacy opting out.
claims.note: The stdio default changed in 2.1.292 at line 286; connector no-flags parity changed in 2.1.295 at line 120.

claims.claim: MCP URL elicitation supports the 2025-11-25 protocol and servers unable to report browser completion wait for "I'm done, continue", while an OAuth scope expansion during a tool call offers reauthentication.
claims.note: URL elicitation was added in 2.1.287 at line 634, including the bareElicitationCapability:true compatibility setting; browser completion and scope prompts changed in 2.1.288.

claims.claim: WebSocket MCP messages larger than 16 MiB close the connection without parsing, matching the limit already applied to other transports.
Keep always-loaded CLAUDE.md instructions below 200 lines and move file-specific instructions into scoped rules.
claims.note: Native memory-O1/O3/O13 already covers loading and the sizing recommendation. BC-lean finds2/2 eligible independent families favor concision; guide and shanraisshan's numeric200-line recommendations count as one vendor lineage, while ykdojo independently recommends simplicity. No numeric quality threshold is measured; matched source trajectories remain unchanged.

claims.claim: The introductory memory module warns against CLAUDE.md files longer than 500 lines.
claims.note: The same pinned guide contains both ceilings; its later lean-file checklist agrees with native memory-O13, so this is an internal documentation correction rather than independent dissent.

claims.claim: Persist task plans, findings and progress in a task-selected project directory so recovery can read durable artifacts after context is cleared.
claims.note: One authored implementation; planning-with-files adapts a declared Manus pattern, and its current recovery deliberately reads the selected project files rather than automatically replaying private agent session stores; native memory-O4 does not itself enforce this three-artifact protocol.

claims.claim: Write reusable learning only for a solved, verified problem whose durable reasoning cannot already be recovered from the final code or documentation.
claims.note: One independent authored policy, not a majority; aligns with keeping instruction content non-derivable under memory-O13; no measured quality gain is established by the policy itself.

claims.claim: Evaluate a generated documentation layer against concrete repository questions before treating it as useful agent context.
claims.note: NirDiamant reports five questions on each of six repositories before and after the layer, improving five repositories and reducing LangChain from 5/5 to 4/5; model pin, repetitions, complete scoring protocol and raw per-question outputs are not supplied in the retained source, so this is source-reported evidence rather than a reproduced universal benefit.

claims.claim: Claude Code concatenates managed, user, project and local CLAUDE.md instructions and loads files from the working directory and its ancestors at startup, while nested instruction files load upon file access.
claims.note: These are instruction files added to model context; this is not a hard policy override mechanism.

claims.claim: A folder's CLAUDE.md is no longer attached a second time after session resume or compaction.
claims.note: This changes instruction duplication and context consumption, rather than introducing a new memory scope.

claims.claim: The /doctor prompt-audit command uses the bundled /claude-api skill to report outdated or conflicting instruction files and proposed edits, and is unavailable when that bundled skill is disabled.
claims.note: The source states it requires 2.1.283 or later; no audit command was run, and no introduction version was inferred without that old CHANGELOG entry.

claims.claim: claudeMdExcludes skips instruction or rule files using absolute-path glob matches with arrays merged across settings scopes, but cannot exclude managed policy CLAUDE.md files.
claims.note: A symlinked rule can be excluded by matching either its .claude/rules path or its target path.

claims.claim: Official memory guidance recommends keeping each CLAUDE.md below 200 lines and moving file-specific instructions into path-scoped rules, while imports improve organization without lowering loaded context cost.
claims.note: This is a size recommendation distinct from MEMORY.md's 200-line/25KB startup cap in memory-O4, and no model-adherence measurement was performed.

claims.claim: CLAUDE.md imports expand @path references at startup, resolve relative paths from the importing file, accept absolute paths and recurse to a maximum depth of four hops.
claims.note: The four-hop limit is the fetched official documentation's wording; no introduced-in version was inferred.

claims.claim: Markdown rules are discovered recursively under .claude/rules, rules without paths frontmatter load at startup, and paths frontmatter restricts a rule to matching files.

Auto memory is stored under ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory with repository worktrees sharing it, and startup loads only the first 200 lines or 25KB of MEMORY.md while detailed topic files remain available on demand.
claims.note: The 200-line/25KB hard startup limit applies to MEMORY.md, whereas the recommendation to keep CLAUDE.md short is separate.

claims.claim: The /memory toggle saves autoMemoryEnabled in user settings, and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1 disables auto memory through the environment.
Auto memory cannot be enabled through /memory in a background session or a session started by Claude Code's own tools, although it can still be disabled there.
Path-scoped rules and nested CLAUDE.md files load when Write or Edit touches their scope and when a single-file cat, head, tail, sed -n or grep command views the file through Bash.
claims.note: Write/Edit loading was corrected in 2.1.288 at line 590; Bash single-file loading was corrected in 2.1.293 at line 184.

claims.claim: Project CLAUDE.md, rule and AGENTS.md symlinks outside the working directories respect permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories and Read deny rules.
claims.note: A documented instruction-loading boundary was corrected; no exploit or runtime test was performed.

claims.claim: Auto-memory loading neutralizes invisible characters and tags resembling Claude Code's internal markup in MEMORY.md and recalled notes before supplying them to the model.
VoltAgent assigns Opus to deep reasoning, Sonnet to everyday coding and Haiku to quick documentation, search and dependency tasks through each subagent's model field.
claims.note: The cost-quality balance is asserted: these lines provide no task sample, comparison protocol, success metric or measured routing result; no effort value is specified.

claims.claim: The guide recommends native opusplan for Opus planning followed by Sonnet implementation.
claims.note: Native model-effort-O1 already implements this alias; the recommendation's superior-planning and lower-cost statements have no source-published matched task-quality evaluation.

claims.claim: Maintained cross-family workflows use Claude to plan or implement and Codex to challenge the plan or review code before continuation.
claims.note: Independent workflow/configuration sources agree on a second model family, but none of these cited passages measures improvement against a single-family baseline; the Shan workflow names Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.4, whereas fcakyon now names GPT-6 Astra.

claims.claim: The templates repository offers Sonnet as the main model, Opus as its advisor and an environment override that forces every subagent to Haiku.
claims.note: This is an available preset, not a measured optimum; it intentionally overrides role-specific agent model choices. Native model-effort-O11/O12 explain advisor context and pairing, and advisor tokens add cost per cost-usage-O4.

claims.claim: Claude Code Harness sets effort by role, using high Fable for difficult decisions, medium Sonnet for ordinary implementation, xhigh Sonnet for its dedicated reviewer and distinct Codex efforts for frontier and worker roles.
claims.note: This is role policy rather than a published quality/per-dollar ranking; task classes and effort are explicit, but no paired benchmark in these lines justifies the mapping. Sonnet 5 and Haiku 4.5 are explicit historical IDs, not current sonnet/haiku aliases.

claims.claim: The pinned guide's table describes Sonnet 5.5 as high effort and Haiku 4.5 as the Haiku family without effort support.
claims.note: L1 at Claude Code 2.1.295 records Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 defaulting to medium and Haiku 5.5 having a native 1M context; this table must not select current alias defaults.

claims.claim: Oh My Claudecode recommends expensive models for rare planning and review calls, cheaper models for implementation and a compatibility-dependent provider choice for each agent.
claims.note: The source explicitly labels this a usage matrix, not a benchmark report; its non-GPT implementation warning is an asserted compatibility observation, not a reproduced result here.

claims.claim: Headroom can opt into reducing reasoning effort on successful tool-result continuation turns while preserving full effort for new questions and errors.
claims.note: HEADROOM_OUTPUT_SHAPER is off by default; the README's separate compression accuracy tables do not measure this effort-routing policy's task quality or savings. L1 model-effort-O10/O15 constrains legacy thinking-budget assumptions on current adaptive families.

claims.claim: Centminmod's model-comparison workflow compares fixed prompt suites using token, cost, cache, tool-call and IFEval-style compliance measures before choosing a model.
claims.note: This is a documented comparison method, not evidence that one particular model route wins; strict format predicates are behavioral compliance signals and do not by themselves prove coding or reasoning quality.

claims.claim: The sonnet, opus and haiku aliases select their latest family models, default clears an override to use the account runtime default, and opusplan uses Opus for planning then Sonnet for execution.
Opus 4.7 and later, Sonnet 5 and later, Haiku 5.5 and Fable always use adaptive reasoning, so fixed thinking-budget mode and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADAPTIVE_THINKING do not apply to those families.
The advisor receives the full conversation and is consulted at model-chosen decision points, while subagents inherit it subject to their own model pairing check.
Since 2.1.287 Sonnet 5.5 can advise Opus 4.7 or 4.8 and unsupported advisor pairings are flagged before requests, while 2.1.295 opens an unavailable saved advisor selection on No advisor.
Ultrathink adds an instruction requesting deeper reasoning for one turn without changing the session or API effort level.
In 2.1.295 skill allowed-tools and effort remain active when the Skill tool finishes before the response stream, fixing denied skill Bash commands in print runs.

Positive MAX_THINKING_TOKENS values do not set a fixed budget on adaptive reasoning models unless adaptive reasoning can be disabled, and zero cannot disable thinking on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 or Fable.

A saved alwaysThinkingEnabled false value has no effect on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 or Fable, whose thinking depth follows effort, but applies again after switching to a model that permits disabling thinking.

The --fallback-model flag accepts an ordered comma-separated fallback chain for unavailable or overloaded primary models, and in 2.1.286 a refusal or fallback retry runs at standard speed when its fallback model cannot run fast.
Thinking is enabled by default where supported, so alwaysThinkingEnabled true changes nothing, while false and MAX_THINKING_TOKENS zero remain subject to the documented model and provider limits.
The 2.1.284 release introduced Sonnet 5.5 as the Anthropic API Sonnet default, and 2.1.293 introduced Haiku 5.5 as the Haiku default, both with native one-million-token context windows.
Current Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 default to medium effort, Opus 4.7 defaults to xhigh, and other effort-capable models default to high unless a higher-precedence choice applies.
claims.note: This is the fetched official default, not a recommendation to replace the host's explicit effort pins.

claims.claim: Explicit environment, CLI or session effort takes precedence over saved model effort and model defaults, and a skill or subagent effort override cannot override CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL or an applicable effort cap.

Low through xhigh can be persisted per model, while max applies only to the current session unless supplied through CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL; 2.1.295 corrected the /model message that wrongly described max as saved.
Since 2.1.284 Ultracode is an independent /effort toggle that remains enabled at any effort level, although --effort ultracode and SDK effortLevel ultracode still enable it with xhigh.
The Agent tool accepts an effort parameter since 2.1.292 to run a subagent at the requested reasoning effort.
Automatic safety fallback preserves the current effort since 2.1.287, and 2.1.290 corrected retries that instead adopted the fallback model's saved effort.
Fast mode uses the same supported Opus model with a speed-prioritized higher-priced API configuration, and fastModePerSessionOptIn makes each session start with it disabled until explicitly enabled.
Select Explanatory or Learning for the desired conversational behavior and retain coding instructions in a coding-oriented custom style.
claims.note: The shanraisshan tip derives from vendor guidance, so these mentions count as one provenance family; native output-styles-O1/O2/O3/O5 already covers style scope, selection and keep-coding-instructions; neither source measures correctness improvement from the preference.

claims.claim: Output styles supply session-wide role, tone, and response-format instructions rather than a guarantee of deterministic actions.
The official built-in style set consists of Default, Proactive, Concise, Explanatory, and Learning.
The output-style command and pickers save the choice to local project settings, the command ignores case, settings values are case-sensitive, and switching takes effect on the next user message.
Custom output styles load from user, project, or managed-policy output-styles directories, with the closest nested project directory winning duplicate names.
Custom output styles omit the full prompt's software-engineering instructions unless keep-coding-instructions is true, and that field has no effect in a shorter prompt that lacks the section.
Output styles affect the main conversation and conversation forks, while ordinary subagents use their own system prompt and do not inherit the style's response instructions.
A plugin style with force-for-plugin true overrides the selected outputStyle and the first loaded enabled plugin wins when several force a style.
Changing output style consults a plugin config.set hook before saving the setting.
The output-style picker opens on the current style, displays each description beneath its name, and no longer selects styles with number keys.
Distribute reusable components through the native marketplace and install the individual plugin required for the role.
claims.note: The guide repeats native plugins-marketplaces-O1/O4 while VoltAgent provides its own supported installation surface; its curated catalog is a pointer source for external agents and is not counted as an efficacy vote; no plugin was installed.

claims.claim: Review plugin hooks, MCP servers and executable dependencies separately from confirming that a plugin directory can load.
claims.note: One authored caution aligned with native component packaging plugins-marketplaces-O1; a --plugin-dir loading example is not a test of supply-chain suitability; reviewed commit pins are source identities, not proof that every documented marketplace can itself be SHA-pinned.

claims.claim: A plugin packages native components including skills, subagents, command hooks, JavaScript hooks modules, and MCP servers under an optional .claude-plugin/plugin.json manifest.
Hooks from claude.ai-synchronized plugins keep working in long-running sessions after another session synchronizes an update rather than failing because the old plugin directory disappeared.

GitHub, URL-repository, and git-subdir plugin sources accept a full forty-character lowercase commit SHA that overrides ref, with direct-SHA hosts requiring a reachable repository commit and other hosts requiring an existing ref from which the pinned commit remains reachable.

Official code-intelligence plugins connect terminal Claude Code to language-server diagnostics and symbol navigation, require a separately installed server binary, and do not start plugin language servers in cloud sessions.

An LSP file assigns each extension to the first registered server, manifest servers can replace same-named file servers, and unresponsive or dynamically registered LSP requests use a configurable 60-second request timeout.
The pinned native security-guidance plugin combines pattern warnings on Edit and Write, model-backed end-of-turn diff review, and an SDK-driven cross-file review before git commits.
claims.note: Source describes this plugin's shipped behavior; the research did not install or execute it.

claims.claim: Plugin LSP initializationOptions and settings receive substituted user_config and CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT values or manifest defaults rather than literal placeholders.

Plugin install scope enables a plugin for a user across projects, for every collaborator through project settings, or locally for one user in one repository, with each collaborator still needing a local installation.
Official and community marketplace names are accepted only for github.com/anthropics repository sources, while all other marketplace names are third-party.

A marketplace lists plugin entry sources in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, relative source paths resolve from the marketplace root, and entry names should match manifest names because installation IDs and skill prefixes use different fields.
Plugin validation rejects marketplace source paths containing parent traversal but a nonexistent source directory is detected during installation rather than validation.
The installed plugin CLI supports component inventory with projected token cost and eval suites against plugin paths or IDs, including a no-plugin baseline arm.
Plugin install, enable, disable, and marketplace-add commands warn when their destination settings file is not loaded.
Marketplace add refuses a marketplace whose name cannot serve as an installable plugin namespace.
Marketplace add and refresh fetch only repository submodules that hold plugin files rather than unrelated large submodules.
Begin with restricted shell filesystem and network access, review violations, and qualify allowed destinations before extending access.
claims.note: Native sandbox-O1/O3/O4/O6 supplies the shell boundary; the second source republishes the vendor's 84% prompt-reduction statistic without quality measurements, so it does not independently validate safety or establish a convergence on that numeric saving.

claims.claim: Use content-matching permission rules for sensitive shell operations because broad Bash ask rules may be skipped during sandbox auto-allow.
claims.note: Native settings-permissions-O15 and sandbox-O5 cover the current rule behavior; the guide reports a 2.1.220 curl demonstration and distinguishes broad ask rules from command-specific ones, but this lane did not reproduce it on 2.1.295.

claims.claim: The shell sandbox is off by default, can be enabled with /sandbox or sandbox.enabled, and is supported on macOS, Linux and WSL2 rather than native Windows.
The sandbox encloses shell commands and their child processes, while built-in file/web tools, MCP servers and hooks run outside it under their separate permission controls.
claims.note: Sandbox denyRead and allowedDomains settings do not directly constrain Read and WebFetch.

claims.claim: Sandbox filesystem policy permits writes to the working and additional directories and the user temporary directory by default, while reads remain broad unless denied or restricted by blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories.
claims.note: The source explicitly warns that default read access can include credential files; no credential was read for this review.

claims.claim: Network isolation routes sandboxed traffic through a host proxy, enforced with Seatbelt on macOS and bubblewrap network isolation on Linux and WSL2.
Sandbox auto-allow and regular-permissions modes enforce the same filesystem and network boundary but differ in whether sandboxed commands need explicit approval, and explicit deny rules still apply.
claims.note: Plan mode, per-command allowed domains, and paths requiring explicit approval have documented exceptions to auto-allow.

claims.claim: Excluded commands and approved unsandboxed retries run outside the sandbox, while managed controls can require sandbox availability and remove the unsandboxed escape hatch.
Project settings cannot widen or disable an admin-required sandbox, replace a proxy protected by managed denials, extend a strict network allowlist or reopen managed filesystem read denials.
The /status and doctor interfaces warn when managed sandbox settings ignore user-configured allowRead paths or allowed domains.
claims.note: The same release warns when a managed settings file links outside its managed folder at line 324, which belongs to settings provenance rather than sandbox enforcement.

claims.claim: Choose a session loop for temporary monitoring and a cloud routine or other durable scheduler for work that must survive a stopped local session.
claims.note: The shanraisshan current tip now says seven days and cloud /schedule; Loop separately chooses cadence and staged rollout by operational purpose; native scheduling-O1/O4/O7/O9 covers lifetimes and persistence, so old memory-only descriptions are not current defaults.

claims.claim: Recurring session tasks expire after three days and remain only in memory until the local process exits.
claims.note: The implementation declares a March 10, 2026 update and the index preserves a March 7 tweet label; the current README:319 already corrects the duration, so scheduling-O4/O7 supersedes the stale pages without proving an across-corpus majority moved.

claims.claim: Roll recurring mutation workflows from report-only through assisted operation to unattended operation only after observing the verifier's recent behavior.
claims.note: One authored rollout policy with a week-long qualification recommendation and recent-run weighting; the retained text does not publish a controlled quality benchmark proving the week is a universal boundary, and native scheduling-O11 provides a separate goal evaluator rather than this rollout policy.

claims.claim: Cloud routines can run without the local machine or an open session, Desktop tasks require the machine but not a session, and session loop tasks require a running local session with one-minute minimum granularity.

The 2.1.290 cloud-session recovery that notified Claude after a container restart lost a pending loop wakeup or scheduled task was reverted in 2.1.293, so the documented release behavior is that the session stays asleep without that notification.

The session goal command uses a separate small-fast-model prompt-based Stop hook to continue until its condition is met or impossible, records the result, and pauses repeated tool-free evaluator loops with the goal still set.
Loop with an explicit interval uses a fixed cron schedule, while a prompt-only loop chooses its next delay dynamically between one minute and one hour.
CronCreate accepts a five-field expression and a recurring or one-shot prompt, CronList and CronDelete manage task IDs, and a session holds at most 50 tasks.

Resume or continue restores eligible CronCreate tasks, but recurring tasks expire after seven days and expired tasks, overdue one-shots, self-paced loops, background Bash, and monitors are not restored.

Scheduled prompts enqueue at low priority between turns in the local timezone, with deterministic recurring jitter of at most half an interval or 30 minutes and up to 90 seconds early jitter for hour-aligned one-shots.

Scheduled fires run only model-invocable skills rather than built-in commands, user-reserved skills, denied skills, or MCP prompts, and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON=1 disables the scheduler and its tools.

Eligible saved scheduled tasks survive compactions made at version 2.1.290 or later and subsequent resume, including after clear or branch creation and after cancellation or rewind, without resurrecting stopped tasks.

Esc stops a backgrounded self-paced loop and announces wakeup cancellation, while Ctrl+C at an attached idle background prompt preserves the pending wakeup so a double press detaches with the loop running.

Research-preview routines save a prompt, repositories, and connectors to run in managed or self-hosted cloud environments through scheduled, API, or repository-event triggers, with custom schedules requiring at least a one-hour interval.
Prefer scoped permission rules or auto mode for ordinary work and reserve permission bypass for an isolated environment.
claims.note: Both repeat vendor safety guidance rather than independently measured alternatives; settings-permissions-O4/O5/O7 covers rule priority, classifier mode and current default; the guide's sandboxed-CI phrase alone does not establish an offline boundary or runtime acceptance.

claims.claim: Configure commit and PR attribution through the attribution settings object when a deterministic change is required.
claims.note: Native settings-permissions-O11/O12 already supplies this mechanism; the tip explicitly credits davila7 and is not an independent extra vote; includeCoAuthoredBy is marked deprecated in the pinned source.

claims.claim: User settings are ~/.claude/settings.json, shared project settings are .claude/settings.json, private project settings are .claude/settings.local.json, and organization settings arrive through managed sources.
claims.note: Private settings are gitignored when Claude Code creates them; a manually created file still needs an explicit ignore entry.

claims.claim: The installed CLI accepts --setting-sources user,project,local to choose settings scopes and --settings <file-or-json> to supply additional session settings.
The attribution setting customizes commit trailers, pull-request text and session links separately, while attribution:false hides all attribution.
claims.note: No introduction date was assigned from current docs alone; the source states that attribution:false requires 2.1.281, outside this delta.

claims.claim: The deprecated includeCoAuthoredBy setting defaults to true and false suppresses commit and PR attribution, but attribution.commit or attribution.pr overrides that legacy switch.
claims.note: The current docs date its deprecation to 2.0.62, but introduced_in remains null because that old tagged CHANGELOG entry was not read here.

claims.claim: autoUpdatesChannel selects latest by default or stable for a release typically about one week old, governs native auto-update and claude update, and can be organization-enforced through managed settings.
claims.note: Homebrew chooses channel by cask name rather than this setting, and WinGet stays on latest.

claims.claim: minimumVersion supplies an updater floor, and changing latest to stable through /config can retain the current version by setting that floor, with returning to latest clearing it.
claims.note: A managed minimumVersion cannot be overridden by user or project settings; no update command was executed.

claims.claim: Content-matching Bash deny and ask rules remain effective under sandbox auto-allow when an expanded environment-variable prefix or a preceding bare variable assignment wraps the command.
claims.note: Current permissions.md lines 645-655 separately explains that the sandbox substitutes for a whole-tool Bash ask rule while content-scoped ask and explicit deny rules still apply.

claims.claim: A dangerous rm targeting a critical path inside a bash -c or sh -c script cannot run without the applicable prompt merely because bypassPermissions or a shell allow rule is active.
claims.note: Current permission-modes.md lines 678-758 documents critical paths and mode-specific outcomes: auto prompts in the terminal and denies elsewhere, dontAsk denies, and default/acceptEdits prompt; this claim does not assert one identical outcome in every interface.

claims.claim: The model is no longer instructed to continue or message subagents through SendMessage when a host, permission rule or --tools list has removed that tool, including after resume.
A subagent or --agent session's local tool omission is no longer announced to the model as though that built-in tool were disabled for the entire session.
claims.note: This concerns scope-correct tool-availability announcements, not a change to a tool allowlist itself.

claims.claim: File path permission checks consult Read(path) and Edit(path) rules, while accepted path rules for Write, NotebookEdit, Glob or legacy MultiEdit are ignored and warned about except a Glob rule supplied through --allowedTools.
claims.note: Use Edit(path) to constrain built-in file-writing tools; this is narrower than a statement that the Write tool can bypass permission controls.

claims.claim: Settings precedence from highest to lowest is managed settings, command-line --settings, project local settings, shared project settings and user settings.
claims.note: Environment variables are not another level in the settings-file stack.

claims.claim: List settings such as permissions.allow combine entries across scopes rather than replacing lower-precedence lists, with the documented model-list exceptions handled separately.
claims.note: The named exceptions are fallbackModel, modelPicker, availableModels, and modelSettings; this claim does not extend ordinary list merging to those keys.

claims.claim: Permission rules resolve in deny, ask, then allow order, so an allow rule cannot override a deny at any settings level or an enforced managed restriction.

Claude Code exposes default/manual, acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk and bypassPermissions modes, with plan withholding edits, auto using classifier review and dontAsk denying calls that would need a prompt.
claims.note: The modes alter approval handling; their individual exceptions remain in the source documentation.

claims.claim: Bash permission patterns match command text with wildcards and account for compound shell operators, while Read and Edit rules constrain file-tool paths and .claudeignore has no permission effect.
claims.note: Shell patterns are not a substitute for OS-level isolation.

claims.claim: Unconfigured interactive terminal and VS Code sessions start in auto mode on all plans and providers, and unconfigured -p and Python Agent SDK sessions on third-party providers or with telemetry disabled use the same default.
claims.note: Interactive parity landed in 2.1.284 at line 1030; non-interactive/Python SDK parity landed in 2.1.285 at line 920; explicit permission-mode settings still override the default.

claims.claim: A repository's project or local settings cannot set CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ATTACHMENTS, while shell, user and managed settings still can.
PreToolUse approvals and auto mode no longer bypass permission prompts for file reads from network UNC paths.
claims.note: This is the CHANGELOG's recorded security correction, not a reproduced security test.

claims.claim: Route a skill with a description stating when it applies and load supporting references or scripts only when the invoked workflow needs them.
claims.note: BC-disclosure reviews7 named current repository READMEs:5/5 eligible authored/provenance families adopt on-demand supporting context, with0 dissent. Guide, shanraisshan and explicitly vendor-derived centminmod text count once; Addy, ShareAI, Claude-mem and Templates contribute package-local adoption policies. These source assertions establish qualitative practice convergence, not independently measured token/cost savings or task-quality gain. Native skills-O11 still covers description routing.

claims.claim: Reserve high-impact manual workflows with disable-model-invocation and review each skill's allowed-tools approvals before enabling it.
claims.note: Native skills-O2/O3 supplies these controls; allowed-tools grants approval for the invoking turn and is not a toolset restriction; one vendor-derived guide, no measured automation threshold.

claims.claim: A skill folder name must match frontmatter name for proper native skill detection.
claims.note: The repository can impose its own naming convention, but its stated native-detection requirement is superseded by skills-O7; this correction does not run or modify any trading skill.

claims.claim: Treat HTML artifact templates as domain instructions supplied to an application workflow rather than as evidence that Claude Code output styles enforce their layout.
claims.note: The eng-runbook template provides frontmatter and layout instructions; HTML Anything declares that its skill protocol mirrors nexu-io/open-design and design constraints derive from huashu-md-html, so it is not an independent additional vote for those copied designs; output-styles-O1 concerns conversation-wide role and tone.

claims.claim: Claude Code 2.1.295 discovers nested <subdir>/.claude/skills: a session started in or below <subdir> loads them at start, and a session started above loads them once Claude works on files there; a name clash shows the nested skill as <dir>:<name>.
claims.note: Claude Code reads .claude/skills; .agents/skills is not found in the CHANGELOG at v2.1.295 nor in the docs' location table. Nested discovery skips gitignored directories (2.1.69).

locators.note: section 'Choose where skills load', row Nested; and the command-name table row for nested clashes

claims.claim: Codex 0.161.0 loads repo-scope skills from <dir>/.agents/skills for every directory between the project root (nearest ancestor with a marker, default .git) and the session's working directory; directories below the working directory are not scanned by this loader.
claims.note: Scope of the absence: no descendant scan in host_roots.rs; the rest of the codex tree was not searched. Applied by the CC on 2026-10-09: trading research Codex lanes launch with their working directory at blueprints/us-equities.

claims.claim: Enterprise skills override same-named personal skills, personal skills override project skills, and plugin skills use a plugin-qualified command namespace.
Skill and custom-command shell injections refuse raw control characters other than tab and newline and identify their location.

Claude selects skills from their description and when_to_use triggers, using the first nonempty body line when description is omitted and applying a default 1536-character listing cap configurable through skillListingMaxDescChars.

The skillOverrides setting defaults absent skills to on and supports on, name-only, user-invocable-only, and off visibility states, with off hiding the skill from model and user command lists and rejecting invocation by its full name.
Setting disable-model-invocation to true reserves a skill for manual invocation and prevents its automatic preload or execution when a scheduled prompt names it.

A skill's allowed-tools grant and effort remain effective throughout its invoking turn, including when the Skill tool finishes before streaming ends, and the tool grant clears on the next user message.
A skill with context: fork runs in a subagent selected by its agent field and defaults to background execution unless background is false.
Hooks declared by a skill register on invocation and remain active for the rest of the session.

A skill's model setting changes the non-fork invoking turn's model without saving settings or selects the child model with context: fork, subject to model allowlists and permission-mode compatibility, while its effort field overrides session effort under the documented resolution order.
Skills whose frontmatter name differs from the containing folder remain invocable by the frontmatter name and the skill listing shows both names.
A compaction summary that repeats a skill command cannot authorize Claude to invoke a user-reserved skill.
When project or user skills contain a skill named verify, Claude's commit guidance calls for invoking it immediately before commits other than changes limited to documentation or tests.
claims.note: This is guidance for a project or user skill named verify; the separate bundled verify skill is documented as user-reserved.

claims.claim: Package frequently repeated inner-loop procedures as skills or commands while keeping host-specific invocation syntax explicit.
claims.note: Native slash-commands-O1/O3 covers legacy command compatibility and plugin namespaces; the community authors agree on reusable named procedures but these skill catalogs are not independent tests of a frequency threshold.
