claims.claim: Legacy custom commands and skills share command behavior, so both .claude/commands/deploy.md and .claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md provide /deploy while legacy files keep working.

The review command is an alias of code-review for diff reviews, and an unspecified low-through-max effort reuses the last interactively selected level while ultra neither uses nor changes that remembered level.

The ultrareview subcommand waits for its cloud review, writes progress to stderr, offers raw bugs JSON and a 45-minute default timeout, and exits zero on completion, one on failure or timeout, and 130 on interruption, whereas print-mode code-review ultra does not wait for findings.

Code-review accepts a remembered max-findings number or all setting resettable with default, and medium effort also reports cleanup and CLAUDE.md convention findings on models without tuned review settings.
The insights command generates an HTML report about recent sessions on the current machine and is unavailable in cloud sessions.
Commands are recognized at the start of a message, with trailing text as arguments, while up to six leading skill invocations can be chained and share the trailing arguments.
Plugin skills expose plugin-qualified slash commands such as /plugin-name:skill-name.
The installed --disable-slash-commands option disables all skills.
Skills substitute the full argument string with ARGUMENTS and support zero-based indexed and shorthand placeholders, preserving shell-quoted multiword arguments.
Skill dynamic shell context executes and substitutes a command's output before Claude receives the skill content.
Replies sent from claude agents arrive as queued messages and slash commands other than stop sent during a running turn execute after the turn ends.
Slash-command descriptions match autocomplete queries by word prefix, improving suggestions when many skills or plugin commands are installed.
Commands that agent view cannot deliver are not silently retained to execute by themselves when the session later restarts.
Use a local JSON-stdin status-line command to display model and workspace information, with refreshInterval only when the display needs time-based updates.
claims.note: One template plus a vendor-derived settings description agree on the native statusline-O1/O9 surface; no local command was executed and no rate-limit, billing or context-total inference is derived from the minimal display.

claims.claim: Status-line context_window total_input_tokens and total_output_tokens represent cumulative token counts across the session.
claims.note: The pinned settings table labels these totals cumulative, which conflicts with native statusline-O3; cost.total_cost_usd is the separately documented session estimate, so the stale label must not drive token-budget accounting.

claims.claim: A statusLine command runs locally with JSON session data on stdin and renders stdout without spending API tokens, subject to workspace trust and the same settings execution gates as hooks.
The status line refreshes at session start and documented session changes, debounces ordinary updates by 300ms and cancels an in-flight script when a new refresh supersedes it.
claims.note: Nonzero exit or empty output blanks the line; changing the command bypasses the debounce.

claims.claim: Status-line context_window totals describe the live context from the latest API response rather than cumulative session spend, and current_usage becomes null before the first response and after compaction until another response arrives.
claims.note: Input totals include fresh input plus cache creation and cache reads; total_output_tokens is the latest response's output.

claims.claim: Status-line cost.total_cost_usd estimates all session API calls, total_duration_ms measures active session wall time across resumes and total_api_duration_ms counts time waiting for responses.
claims.note: These are estimated API-equivalent counters; they do not themselves measure a subscription bill.

claims.claim: Claude apps gateway spend limits display dollar usage in /usage and the status line and expose used_usd, limit_usd and period in rate_limits.spend_limit when the gateway version supports it.
claims.note: The gateway must run this release or later for the displayed dollar amounts; no gateway endpoint was queried.

claims.claim: Status-line rate_limits supplies subscriber five_hour and seven_day usage/reset windows or gateway spend_limit fields, with dollar fields fetched on a slower schedule than percentages.
claims.note: Scripts must handle absent or null values; the supplied documentation separates ordinary response-time percentages from periodically fetched dollar values.

claims.claim: The subagentStatusLine payload includes agentType so scripts can distinguish custom subagent types.
subagentStatusLine receives all visible tasks in a tasks array once per refresh and overrides chosen rows with JSON lines containing id and content.
claims.note: Omitting a task id keeps that task's default row; the normal trust and hook gates also apply.

claims.claim: statusLine.refreshInterval optionally reruns the command every N seconds with a one-second minimum, keeping time-based or background-driven values refreshed while the main session is idle.
claims.note: Leaving it unset retains event-driven refresh only.

claims.claim: Delegate focused work with explicit ownership and separate context or worktrees when concurrent tasks can otherwise collide.
claims.note: Three authored designs agree on scoped ownership/isolation after counting the guide as one family; native subagents-teams-O1/O7/O9 covers separate contexts, worktrees and team messaging; AO's own workspaces do not replace native Claude workers, as the bounded AO adoption record requires.

claims.claim: Scale delegation to task isolation and result collection rather than treating the phrase use subagents as a sufficient reason to spawn more workers.
claims.note: The sources dissent on emphasis: the shanraisshan tip advocates extra compute, while the guide says a single bounded Agent call needs no workflow wrapper; native subagents-teams-O1/O8 distinguishes ordinary children from experimental interactive teams; no optimal teammate count is measured.

claims.claim: Subagents run delegated work in a separate context and inherit available tools unless tools restricts them, while disallowedTools removes the matching whole tool.
In-process teammates are not restored by resume or rewind, cannot create nested teams, and cannot run their own subagents in the background.

Conversation forks inherit the parent's conversation, system prompt, tools, and model, while an explicit Agent-tool effort override is documented for non-fork agents and persists on resume below the environment effort override.

A named teammate uses the selected definition's tools and uses its model when the spawn prompt names no model, applies the definition's effort to in-process teammates, and ignores its skills field, while an Agent call that passes isolation or requests a fork remains an ordinary subagent.
claims.note: The read teammate applicability list does not state that omitClaudeMd is applied; no stronger omission guarantee is inferred.

claims.claim: A subagent's omitClaudeMd setting omits user, project, and local CLAUDE.md while retaining managed policy except for managed subagents, and the setting is ignored when the agent runs as the main session agent.
A forked subagent preserves the parent's permission mode, including plan and dontAsk, and cannot exit plan mode.
A plugin-defined named teammate uses its definition's prompt, tools, disallowedTools, and effort instead of teammate defaults.
Plugin-defined subagents ignore hooks, mcpServers, and permissionMode frontmatter; plugin-level hooks and MCP servers instead apply whenever the plugin is enabled.
Subagent definitions require name and description in YAML frontmatter and place their system prompt in the following Markdown body, with unrecognized frontmatter fields ignored without an error.
The skills field preloads full skill content at startup once each for at most 32 skills, without limiting later Skill-tool access to the other invocable skills.
Subagent frontmatter effort overrides session effort below CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL, and the Agent tool accepts an explicit effort parameter for a delegated agent.
A subagent definition requesting permissionMode: auto does not enter auto mode when settings, the circuit breaker, or the selected model makes auto mode unavailable.
Background subagent permission prompts surface in the main session, session-length grants apply to the whole session, and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1 forces foreground execution.

Subagent memory can persist at user, project, or local scope, and experimental.cacheTtl accepts 5m or 1h for that subagent while unsupported values and 1h during subscription usage credits are ignored.
Setting subagent isolation to worktree creates a temporary isolated checkout based by default on the default branch and removes it automatically when no changes are made.
Agent teams are experimental and disabled by default, require CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1, and spawn teammates only in interactive sessions rather than -p or Agent SDK runs.
An agent team gives a fixed lead and independently contextualized teammates a shared task list and direct mailbox messaging.
